newsitem.title: UK: BP says Q3 oil price benefit $400/500 mln.
newsitem.headline: BP says Q3 oil price benefit $400/500 mln.

text.p: British Petroleum Co Plc said on Tuesday that its third-quarter earnings were boosted by a gain of $400 to 500 million stg from higher oil prices.
But group chief executive John Browne told reporters following publication of results that the benefit was offset by pressure on profit margins in its downstream operations and chemicals.
The crude oil price averaged around $22 a barrel in the third quarter, around 2 1/2 above the price a year before.
"We think that for the fourth quarter prices will remain relatively favourable at about $22," Browne said.
Browne said current demand was strong, adding "we expect quite strong demand next year." But he said the timing of the return to the market of Iraqi exports remained "a wild card."

BP said the results of its "self help" measures were adding around $150 million of profits per quarter, while the current strength of sterling against the dollar was not likely to have a serious impact on earnings. The company said a rate of $1.65 to the pound would reduce quarterly profits by around $15 million.
Browne said it would "be some time" before BP made announcements on the sale of its Lima refinery in Ohio, and French refinery at Lavera, announced in January.

But Browne said that BP's record third quarter net earnings on a cost replacement basis, which rose 22 percent to 650 million stg, were the result of "self help" rather than the oil price, with cost-cutting and greater efficiency all boosting the bottom line.

BP said its return on capital employed was currently the best in the industry at 17 percent in the nine months through September. "Many large competitors are struggling at this stage of the cycle to reach 12 percent" said Browne.
BP rival Royal Dutch/Shell Group has a return on capital of just below 12 percent, while the general range in the industry is currently 12 to 15 percent.
Chairman Sir David Simon said, however, that these levels "are not easily sustainable, particularly when you see inflation levels at three to four percent worldwide."

Browne added that BP was now "much less vulnerable" to changes in the oil price. He said the group's long-term view that the oil price will settle back into the $16 to $18 per barrell range "has not changed."
"The question is how we'll get from here to there," he said.
"Selling refineries is a tough business," he said.
